rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 0 (kp 3.5, kd 0.15, ki 0.05, base 1.5, 12 mm sensors at y=0.06) remains the best-scoring design at 53.02. Iteration 2 (16 mm sensors) fell to 50.49, so the larger footprint is rejected. Iteration 3 (kp 2.5) fell to 35.52, so lowering kp clearly hurts. Iteration 1 (kp 4.0 with ki 0.4 and kd 0.2) scored 50.62, but it changed three factors, so it is not a clean test of kp 4.0. Every run in all iterations ended off track at progress 0.04 to 0.15, and the s-bend progress of 0.1475 has not moved under any kp from 3.5 to 4.5.

What I kept, changed and rejected after the round-2 critique:
(1) Kept the iteration 0 geometry exactly, with 12 mm sensors and no footprint change. This removes the blur risk the critique raised for 16 mm sensors.
(2) Kept the single change kp 3.5 to 4.0 from my revision. The critique's main point is that this test is close to a null, and I accept that. kp 4.0 is still the only lever with a clean measured effect (2.5 is much worse, so kp matters at least below 3.5). The test is clean for kp alone, so I keep it.
(3) Accepted the critique's request for quantified thresholds. The result will be read on the three-track mean score and on progress per track. Support for kp 4.0 requires a mean score above 53.0 and the s-bend progress above 0.1475, or oval progress above 0.1355 with no oval-only driver. Anything within about 0.5 of 53.0 is treated as noise, because iteration 0's oval spread was 48.3 to 74.9.
(4) Rejected the critique's suggestion to change sensor placement or track-related geometry. The data do not show what would move the early failure point (about 0.1 to 0.15 of the course), and changing geometry now would again remove attribution.
(5) Rejected a speed cut. Completion needs about 1.5 m/s average, and no evidence shows speed is the limit. Speed will be tested alone later if the failure point stays fixed.
(6) Rejected the critique's proposal to move to line_loss search_right next. The data do not link line loss to the early failure, so it is not the next lever.

Decision rule for the next revision: if the mean score exceeds 53.0 and the s-bend progress exceeds 0.1475, keep kp 4.0 and test kd alone (0.15 to 0.4). If the score falls below 52.5, revert to kp 3.5 and test kd alone. If the s-bend progress stays at 0.1475 with the score within 0.5 of 53.0, kp does not set the failure point, and the next test is kd alone. If progress exceeds 0.9 with completion 0, raise base_speed by 0.1.

Expected result: score within about 1 point of 53.0, with max_error near 0.06 m. A large gain is not expected from one gain change.
